answer: Cross-verification panels can expose cloned agents. A beacon-derived seed assigns each new identity to one shard of the orchard, overlapping its task with unlikely peers. Panels compare responses item by item: genuine agents diverge in style, errors, and timing, while sybil clones from one process correlate. Detected correlation slashes every implicated stake, and the raven audit log publishes the matrix on-chain so any peer can rerun the test cheaply. Attackers must then generate independent cognition per identity, costing more than honest participation and scaling linearly with clones.
